subject: history

items.q: How did Hitler first become Chancellor in 1933?
items.correct: He was legally appointed Chancellor by President Hindenburg.
items.misconception: He seized power in a violent revolution.
items.random_wrong: He won an outright majority in a free election.
items.why: The 1923 Munich Putsch had failed; in 1933 Hitler was appointed, then dismantled democracy from within.

items.q: Did the Nazis ever win a majority in a free election?
items.correct: No — they peaked at about 37% (July 1932) and never won an outright majority freely.
items.misconception: Yes, they won over 50% in a free election.
items.random_wrong: They were never voted for at all.
items.why: The Nazis were the largest party but relied on backroom deals and then terror to take full power.

items.q: Was the Weimar Republic a failure from start to finish?
items.correct: No — it had a recovery and cultural 'Golden Age' under Stresemann (1924–29).
items.misconception: Yes, it failed continuously with no successes.
items.random_wrong: It lasted only a few months.
items.why: After early crises (hyperinflation 1923), Weimar stabilised in the mid-1920s before the Depression hit.
